key_insight: SimAuthor turns foundation-model outputs into persistently revised scientific simulators, improving executable biomedical modeling under weak real-world feedback.
clinical_relevance: Better simulators for ECG, PPG, and cardiopulmonary signals could support more realistic synthetic data generation and stronger downstream model development in medical imaging and sensing.
method: Keeps an executable simulator rather than only generating samples.
Uses distributional comparison between simulated and real signals plus structured discrepancy feedback.
Accumulates reusable implementation changes across iterative revisions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on six biomedical tasks with a fixed 100-attempt budget; SimAuthor beat PUCT on all six tasks, achieved the top final score on five, and improved downstream ECG classification out of distribution.
watch_item: Results depend on limited empirical feedback and task-specific evaluation, so performance may not generalize without careful validation on new modalities or datasets.
paper_title: SimAuthor: Harnessing Foundation Models for Persistent Scientific Simulator Authoring
